To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a semi-mechanistically motivated pharmacodynamic (PD) model for neutropenic response to the polo-like kinase  (Plk-1) inhibitor BI 253 6 and applied it in a clinical development program.
a semi-mechanistics population PK/PD model for neutropenic response was applied to describe neutropenic effects following therapy with BI 2536 in patients with cancer.
we have developed a population pharmacokinetic model for BI 2536 that describes the neutropenic effect of this drug.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drugs, the design of new drugs, and the development of new drug delivery systems.
the development and validation of mathematical models to describe the neutro- and thrombopenic effects of the Plk- 1 inhibitor BI 2525.
the development of a semi-mechanistically based population model to describe the neutrophil response to BI 2536, a Plk-1-inhibitor.

the model is a useful tool for dose finding and dose individualisation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutropenia of BI 2535 is not dose limiting.
the neutropenic risk can be reduced by shortening the treatment duration from 3 to only 2 weeks without increasing neutropenic risk.
